before_objects.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
before_objects.statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of the affine Minkowski space A and let n: Omega -> V be an observer congruence with acceleration a := nabla_n n, expansion tensor theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and rest metric h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a)-(c), def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space). (a) Material family and material metric. Let J be a nonempty open interval, B a nonempty open subset of R^3, and Phi: J x B -> Omega a smooth map with partial Phi/partial s = n(Phi(s,xi)) for all (s,xi) in J x B; assume that Phi is an injective immersion (its derivative is injective at every point), so that the four vector fields n, e_1, e_2, e_3 are linearly independent, where e_I := partial Phi/partial xi^I, I = 1,2,3. Define the material metric G_{IJ}(s,xi) := h(e_I,e_J) evaluated at Phi(s,xi). Then G is symmetric, and for every s the matrix (G_{IJ}) is positive definite, so that G(.,.) is a Riemannian metric on B for each s; moreover (s,xi) |-> G_{IJ}(s,xi) is smooth. (b) Evolution of rest separations. For all I,J and every (s,xi) one has d/ds G_{IJ} = (L_n h)(e_I,e_J) = 2 theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b, equivalently d/dtau G_{IJ} = 2 c theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b, where tau = s/c is the proper time of the congruence worldlines (the flow lines of n have four-velocity c n). If additionally I = J and e_I is nowhere zero on the family, then with |e_I|_h := sqrt(h(e_I,e_I)) and u := e_I/|e_I|_h one has d/dtau |e_I|_h = c theta(u,u) |e_I|_h: the fractional rate of change, per unit proper time, of the rest length of the material element in the direction e_I is c theta(u,u), positive where the expansion is positive and negative where it is negative. (c) Born rigidity. If theta = 0 on Omega, i.e. the congruence is Born rigid, then G is constant along the flow, d/ds G_{IJ}(s,xi) = 0 for all I,J,s,xi and with no restriction on the separation: a Born-rigid material continuum preserves its internal metric exactly. Conversely, if theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b is nonzero at some point of the family, then the corresponding component G_{IJ} is not constant there. (d) Scope. Everything is local on the given smooth family and uses only the flat connection and the congruence kinematics. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem or boundary condition is used, and no choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Differentiate the material metric along the flow. By construction e_I = Phi_* partial_{xi^I} and n = Phi_* partial_s are pushforwards of the commuting coordinate fields of J x B, so [n,e_I] = 0 (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields, prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket). For any (0,2) tensor field K and vector fields X,Y the Lie derivative identity (L_X K)(Y,Z) = X(K(Y,Z)) - K([X,Y],Z) - K(Y,[X,Z]) together with [n,e_I] = [n,e_J] = 0 gives d/ds [h(e_I,e_J)] = n(h(e_I,e_J)) = (L_n h)(e_I,e_J) (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). Clause (d) of def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics states (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, hence d/ds G_{IJ} = 2 theta_{ab} e_I{}^a e_J{}^b. The proper-time form uses d/dtau = c d/ds: the flow is parametrized by s with dx/ds = n, so the four-velocity is c n and ds = c dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, def-sr-proper-time, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)). The length statement is the chain rule applied to |e_I|_h^2 = h(e_I,e_I): d/ds |e_I|_h = (1/(2|e_I|_h)) 2 theta(e_I,e_I) = |e_I|_h theta(u,u) with u := e_I/|e_I|_h and theta(u,u) = theta(e_I,e_I)/|e_I|_h^2 (def-derivative, thm-algebra-of-derivatives, thm-chain-rule). Positive definiteness: h is symmetric with radical spanned by n and positive definite on n^perp (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a)); for v = v^I e_I nonzero and not parallel to n one has h(v,v) > 0, so G is positive definite, and no v^I e_I can be parallel to n because n, e_1, e_2, e_3 are linearly independent by the injective-immersion hypothesis. Smoothness of (s,xi) |-> G_{IJ} follows from smoothness of Phi, of n and of the bilinear form eta (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, def-sr-affine-minkowski-model). The Born-rigid case is the vanishing of theta. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Bell's rockets and thread: constant chart-frame separation of equal chart-frame accelerations with nonvanishing longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence
before_objects.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions for the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let J be an open interval containing 0, let q: J -> R be C^2 with |q'(t)| < c for every t in J, put gamma(t) := (1 - q'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, let L > 0 and a real pair y_0, z_0 be given, and consider the two rocket worldlines x_0(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t), y_0, z_0) and x_L(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + L, y_0, z_0), t in J. Consider also an idealized thread whose material points are labelled by xi in an open interval containing [0,L] and whose element labelled xi moves on the worldline x_xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + xi, y_0, z_0). Then: (a) Kinematics of the rockets. x_0 and x_L are C^2 future timelike worldlines with four-velocity U_xi(t) = gamma(t) (c, q'(t), 0, 0) (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(e)); the two rockets have equal chart-frame velocity q'(t) at every chart time and their chart-frame separation is the constant q(t) + L - q(t) = L, so their chart-frame accelerations q''(t) are equal as well. (b) The translated congruence and its expansion. On the open set covered by the worldlines, n := gamma(t) (1, q'(t)/c, 0, 0) is a smooth future unit timelike field whose flow lines are the worldlines x_xi (which are translated members of one another); it is the translated congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d), whose unit longitudinal rest vector is s := gamma (q'/c, 1, 0, 0) and whose expansion along s is theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (c)); this quantity is nonzero exactly at parameter values with q'(t) q''(t) nonzero, and it changes sign with q'q''. (c) Rest separation versus chart separation. The material field e := partial_xi is the unit chart displacement e = (0,1,0,0); its rest length per unit label is |e|_h = sqrt(h(e,e)) = gamma(t), and the rest separation between the two rockets, measured with the material metric of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching along the flow, is |e|_h L = gamma(t) L. By that lemma the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is c theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^2, so d(gamma L)/dtau = gamma^4 L q' q''/c^2 and, in particular, whenever q'(t) = v at some time, the rest separation at that time equals L/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) > L if v != 0, with minimum L exactly at parameter values with q' = 0. Thus the chart-frame separation L is constant while the rest separation gamma(t) L is not. (d) Material reading of the thread. If a thread attached to the rockets is modelled by material points following the flow lines of n (each thread element moving with the locally coincident rocket), then by lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching its internal longitudinal material metric component is G_11 = gamma(t)^2 and its own rest-length measure between the two endpoint elements grows from L to gamma(t) L; whenever q'(t) != 0 the thread is stretched relative to its initial length by the factor gamma(t) > 1. A conclusion that an actual thread breaks or is under a definite tension requires an elasticity model with a failure or constitutive criterion; no such model is specified here, and no breaking or tension conclusion is drawn from the kinematic computation alone. (e) Contrast with Born rigidity. The Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) is Born rigid, its neighbouring worldlines have constant rest separation, and its proper accelerations c^2/rho are unequal (def-sr-proper-acceleration); conversely the translated congruence has equal chart-frame velocity and acceleration profiles along its members but is not Born rigid wherever q'q'' != 0. Born rigidity of a congruence is therefore not equivalent to equality of the chart-frame accelerations of its members, and constant chart separation of a family of worldlines is not the constancy of their rest separation. (f) Scope. This is a conditional kinematic deduction in flat classical spacetime about the specified worldlines and the specified material reading of the thread; it contains no dynamics, no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about real threads or real rockets. No choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Direct computation with the translated congruence. (a) Differentiating x_xi with the chain rule gives (c, q'(t), 0, 0) = (c/gamma) gamma(1, q'/c, 0, 0); its eta-norm is c^2/gamma^2 . (-1 + q'^2/c^2) = -c^2, so it is future timelike and the four-velocity is gamma(c, q', 0, 0) (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets); the chart separation is q(t) + L - q(t) = L by construction. (b) The expansion formula is clause (d) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples, which also identifies n, s and the field; the vanishing statement is the product rule for q'q''. (c) With e = (0,1,0,0) one has eta(n,e) = gamma q'/c and h(e,e) = eta(e,e) + eta(n,e)^2 = 1 + gamma^2 q'^2/c^2 = gamma^2 (gamma^{-2} + q'^2/c^2) = gamma^2 (1 - q'^2/c^2 + q'^2/c^2) = gamma^2, so |e|_h = gamma; the rest separation is |e|_h L by linearity of the material metric along the (constant) label direction, and the evolution is the length clause of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching with u = e/|e|_h = s. The chain-rule identity d gamma/dtau = gamma^4 q'q''/c^2 follows from d gamma/dt = gamma^3 q'q''/c^2 and dtau = dt/gamma, and agrees with the expansion form; the evaluation at a time with q' = v is a substitution. (d) The material metric G_11 = h(e,e) = gamma^2 is the thread's own longitudinal metric by lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a), and its growth is clause (b) of that lemma; the elasticity caveat is part of the statement and is not proved, because no elasticity model is available or claimed. (e) The Rindler facts are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) together with def-sr-proper-acceleration (b), and the non-rigidity of the translated congruence is (b) above. (f) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before_objects.title: Bell congruence worked: rest separation grows as gamma(t)L while the chart separation stays constant
before_objects.statement: Worked computation for the Bell congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d) and the material metric of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching. Fix c > 0 and alpha > 0, let J := (-c/alpha, c/alpha), put q(t) := (1/2) alpha t^2 on J and let x_xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + xi, 0, 0) for xi in an open interval containing [0,L], L > 0, in the inertial chart x with x^0 = c t. Then |q'(t)| = alpha|t| < c on the two-sided domain J; write beta(t) := alpha t/c and gamma(t) := (1 - beta(t)^2)^{-1/2}. (a) The translated congruence field is n = gamma (1, beta, 0, 0) and the material field e := partial_xi is the constant (0,1,0,0); since eta(n,e) = gamma beta, the h-length of e is |e|_h = sqrt(eta(e,e) + eta(n,e)^2) = sqrt(1 + gamma^2 beta^2) = gamma(t) (lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a), thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d)). Hence the rest separation between the rockets labelled 0 and L is |e|_h L = gamma(t) L > L for every t != 0, with minimum L at t = 0, while the chart-frame separation is q(t) + L - q(t) = L for every t in J. (b) The longitudinal expansion of the translated congruence is theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3, with unit rest vector s = gamma(beta,1,0,0) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d)); it vanishes at t = 0 and is nonzero for every t != 0, negative for t < 0 and positive for t > 0. By lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (b) the internal longitudinal material metric component is G_11 = h(e,e) = gamma(t)^2 and its derivatives are d/ds G_11 = 2 theta(e,e) and d/dtau G_11 = 2 c theta(e,e); equivalently the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is d/dtau log(gamma L) = c theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^2, and d(gamma L)/d tau = gamma^4 L alpha^2 t/c^2. (c) Explicit check at alpha t = 3c/5, i.e. t = 3c/(5alpha) in J: beta = 3/5, gamma = 5/4 and sinh and cosh are not needed; the rest separation is 5L/4 > L, the internal metric component is G_11 = 25/16 > 1, the expansion is theta(s,s) = (125/64)(3alpha/(5c^2)) = 75alpha/(64c^2), and the fractional rest-separation rate is c theta(s,s) = 75alpha/(64c). At t = 0 the rest separation takes its minimum L and the expansion vanishes; the domain is the two-sided interval (-c/alpha, c/alpha), so both the decelerating branch t < 0 (negative expansion) and the accelerating branch t > 0 (positive expansion) are included. (d) Scope. The computation is exact kinematics of the specified family: it uses no elasticity, no material failure criterion, no force law, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it draws no conclusion about real threads; no choice principle is used.
before_objects.strategy: Direct evaluation of the family in the two-sided subluminal domain. (a) Differentiating the members with the chain rule gives tangent (c, q'(t), 0, 0) = (c/gamma) n, so the flow field is n = gamma(1, beta, 0, 0) and each member is future timelike (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, thm-chain-rule); the h-length computation is eta(e,e) = 1 and eta(n,e) = gamma beta, whence h(e,e) = 1 + gamma^2 beta^2 = gamma^2 (1 - beta^2 + beta^2) = gamma^2 by gamma^{-2} = 1 - beta^2 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (a), lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching (a)). (b) The expansion formula is clause (d) of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples; the material-metric statements are clauses (b) and (c) of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching applied to e, with theta(e,e) = gamma^2 theta(s,s) because e = |e|_h s = gamma s. The logarithmic rate identity follows from d/dtau = (gamma/c) d/dt and d gamma/dt = gamma^3 beta beta' = gamma^3 q'q''/c^2 (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative). (c) Substituting alpha t = 3c/5 gives beta = 3/5, gamma^{-2} = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25, gamma = 5/4, gamma^2 = 25/16, and theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3 = (125/64)(alpha^2 (3c/(5alpha))/c^3) = (125/64)(3alpha/(5c^2)) = 75alpha/(64c^2), so c theta(s,s) = 75alpha/(64c); the remaining values are substitutions. (d) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

proposed_subjects.title: The material metric of a congruence: evolution of rest separations and preservation of the internal metric under Born rigidity
proposed_subjects.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of affine Minkowski space $A$, $c>0$, and let $n:\Omega\to V$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field, $\eta(n,n)=-1$. Define the following first-order quantities in any inertial chart:
$$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,\qquad h_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b,\qquad a^b:=n^c\partial_cn^b,\qquad\theta_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)},$$
where symmetrization means half the sum, $n_a:=\eta_{ab}n^b$, and $h(v,w):=h_{ab}v^aw^b$. Here $h$ is $C^1$ and $a,\theta$ are continuous. The rest projection $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c). For $C^1$ fields and tensors define
$$(L_nh)_{ab}:=n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c.$$
These first-order coordinate formulas transform tensorially under affine inertial chart changes and agree, on smooth fields, with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] and the ordinary smooth Lie derivative. Say the $C^1$ field is Born rigid when $L_nh=0$; the identity $L_nh=2\theta$ makes this equivalent to $\theta=0$.
(a) Let $J$ be a nonempty open interval, $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open set, and $\Phi:J\times B\to\Omega$ an injective $C^2$ immersion with $\partial_s\Phi=n(\Phi)$. Put $e_I:=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $I=1,2,3$, and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi):=h(e_I,e_J)$ at $\Phi(s,\xi)$. Then $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are linearly independent, $G$ is symmetric positive definite at every point, and its entries are $C^1$. Thus for each $s$ it is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric on $B$. If $n$ and $\Phi$ are smooth, $G$ is a smooth Riemannian metric, as in the original smooth branch.
(b) For all $I,J$,
$$\partial_sG_{IJ}=(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)=2\theta(e_I,e_J),\qquad\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J),$$
where $\tau=s/c$ is the proper-time parameter along each flow line, whose four-velocity is $cn$. For a nonzero label direction $e_I$, put $\ell_I:=\sqrt{h(e_I,e_I)}>0$ and $u_I:=h(e_I)/\ell_I$. This $u_I$ is a horizontal unit rest vector, and
$$\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I.$$
The alternative normalized material vector $e_I/\ell_I$ need not be horizontal, but has the same $\theta$ contraction because $\theta$ is horizontal. Positive/negative expansion gives positive/negative fractional change of this material rest length per proper time.
(c) If $\theta=0$, then $\partial_sG_{IJ}=0$ and $G_{IJ}(s,\xi)$ is constant in $s$ for each fixed label, with no restriction on material-label separation: the entire internal metric is preserved exactly. Conversely, a nonzero contraction $\theta(e_I,e_J)$ gives a nonzero derivative of that metric component at the point and hence nonconstancy on a neighborhood. The smooth Born-rigid branch and its original conclusions are included.
(d) This is a local statement about the given family and its material metric. Integrating the material metric at a common flow parameter gives an internal label-space length; it does not identify that length with a finite endpoint distance on a single observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane without an additional argument. No matter model, elasticity, field equation, global rigidity theorem, boundary condition or choice principle is used.
proposed_subjects.strategy:
Use only first derivatives of $n$ and two derivatives of $\Phi$. The coordinate rules are tensorial under constant Lorentz changes of inertial coordinates by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]; for smooth data they agree with the established smooth definitions. Differentiating $\eta(n,n)=-1$ gives $n_b\partial_an^b=0$, hence $\eta(n,a)=0$. Expansion of the projected symmetrization gives
$$2\theta_{ab}=\partial_an_b+\partial_bn_a+n_aa_b+a_an_b.$$
Differentiating $h_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b$ in the displayed first-order Lie formula gives exactly this right side, proving $L_nh=2\theta$. The projectors make $\theta$ horizontal in both slots.
For the material fields, equality of the mixed partials of $C^2$ components of $\Phi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the total chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) give
$$\partial_se_I^a=\partial_{\xi^I}n^a(\Phi)=(\partial_bn^a)(\Phi)e_I^b.$$
Differentiating $G_{IJ}=h_{ab}(\Phi)e_I^ae_J^b$ by the product rule gives the displayed coordinate formula for $(L_nh)(e_I,e_J)$, and thus $\partial_sG_{IJ}=2\theta(e_I,e_J)$. This direct calculation does not invoke a smooth-only Lie-bracket supplier for $C^1$ fields. In the smooth branch, the same mixed-partial identity is the usual commuting material-coordinate calculation $[n,e_I]=0$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]), and recovers the original smooth route.
The derivative of $\Phi$ has four independent columns by immersion, so no nonzero linear combination of the three $e_I$ lies in $\operatorname{span}(n)$. The rest projection has that one-dimensional kernel and is positive definite on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c)); hence $G$ is positive definite. $h(\Phi)$ and $e_I$ are $C^1$, so $G$ is $C^1$, and smooth if all data are smooth. Along a flow line $\partial_s\Phi=n$ is nonzero future timelike, and the proper-time definition gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-\eta(n,n)}/c=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Apply the chain rule to $\ell_I^2=G_{II}$: $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(e_I,e_I)/\ell_I$. Since $h(e_I)-e_I$ is parallel to $n$, horizontality gives $\theta(e_I,e_I)=\ell_I^2\theta(u_I,u_I)$, proving the fractional-rate formula. If $\theta=0$, the interval zero-derivative corollary [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] proves constancy for each fixed label. A nonzero derivative prevents local constancy. All claims, including the smooth special case, are proved with the stated finite regularity and no zero tangent is called timelike.

proposed_subjects.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$ of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $J$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $q:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ with $|q\prime(t)|<c$, set $\beta=q\prime/c$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $L>0$, and fix transverse coordinates $(y_0,z_0)$. The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.
(a) Every member is $C^2$ future timelike: its chart-time tangent is $(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2/\gamma^2<0$. Its common proper-time function is $\tau(t):=\int_0^t\gamma(v)^{-1}dv$, and its proper four-velocity is $U=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$ with squared norm $-c^2$. All members have equal chart velocity and acceleration, $q\prime,q\prime\prime$, and their chart separation is the constant $L$.
(b) The four-dimensional extension is essential for applying the material-family lemma. Choose open transverse intervals $Y,Z$ containing $y_0,z_0$, put $\sigma:=c\tau$, let $t=t(\sigma)$ be the inverse on $c\tau(J)$, and set
$$\Phi(\sigma,\xi,y,z):=x^{-1}(ct(\sigma),q(t(\sigma))+\xi,y,z),\qquad(\xi,y,z)\in B:=I\times Y\times Z.$$
This is an injective $C^2$ immersion onto an open set, with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ and $\partial_\sigma\Phi=n(\Phi)$, where $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a $C^1$ future unit field. Apply the first-order definitions in [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]], which agree with [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] when smooth. The longitudinal unit rest vector is $s_\parallel:=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$, and
$$\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3.$$
This agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d), is nonzero exactly where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$, and changes sign with that product. When $q$ is smooth the full original smooth-congruence branch is recovered. Restricting the extension to fixed $y_0,z_0$ gives the prescribed thread.
(c) For its material label tangent $e=\partial_\xi\Phi=(0,1,0,0)$, $h(e,e)=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)/\gamma=s_\parallel$. The vector $e/\gamma$ generally is not $s_\parallel$, but horizontality implies $\theta(e/\gamma,e/\gamma)=\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)$. The internal longitudinal material metric is $G_{11}=\gamma^2$, so its length at common flow parameter is
$$\mathcal L(t):=\int_0^L\sqrt{G_{11}}d\xi=\gamma(t)L.$$
It is an internal material metric length, not automatically the finite endpoint distance on one observer's orthogonal simultaneity hyperplane. The local evolution is
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}\log\mathcal L=c\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2,\qquad\frac{d\mathcal L}{d\tau}=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2.$$
At a time with $q\prime=v$, $\mathcal L=L/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\ge L$, with equality exactly for $v=0$. Chart separation stays $L$; the material length is constant precisely when $q\prime{}^2$ is constant, and has nonzero local rate wherever $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$.
(d) Under the stipulated material reading that thread elements follow these flow lines, the initial internal length is $\gamma(0)L$ and its relative factor is $\gamma(t)/\gamma(0)$. Relative to that initial state it stretches where $\gamma(t)>\gamma(0)$, shrinks where $\gamma(t)<\gamma(0)$, and has equal length where the factors agree. In the special initially resting case $q\prime(0)=0$, the initial length is $L$ and every state with $q\prime(t)\ne0$ has stretch factor $\gamma(t)>1$. No elasticity or failure criterion is supplied, so neither breaking nor a definite tension of an actual thread follows.
(e) The Rindler congruence in [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](b) is Born rigid, with constant internal rest separations and unequal proper accelerations $c^2/\rho$ at distinct radial labels ([[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]). Equal chart-velocity and acceleration profiles in the translated family do not imply Born rigidity where $q\prime q\prime\prime\ne0$. Constant chart separation and constant internal rest metric are distinct kinematic conditions.
(f) This is a conditional flat-spacetime deduction for prescribed worldlines and the stated material reading. It assumes no dynamical or elastic model, force law, material failure criterion, measurement or empirical fact, and asserts nothing about real threads or rockets. No choice principle is used.
proposed_subjects.strategy:
(a) Differentiate the given worldlines. The chart-time tangent has norm $-c^2+q\prime{}^2=-c^2/\gamma^2$ and positive time component, so it is nonzero future timelike. Proper time gives $d\tau/dt=1/\gamma$ and $U=dx/d\tau=\gamma(c,q\prime,0,0)$; its norm is $-c^2$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). The separation and equality of chart derivatives follow directly.
(b) Since $q$ is $C^2$, $\gamma$ is $C^1$ and $\tau\prime=1/\gamma$ is positive $C^1$, so $\tau$ is $C^2$ and strictly increasing. [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]] gives its $C^1$ inverse; its derivative $dt/d\tau=\gamma(t(\tau))$ is $C^1$, hence the inverse is $C^2$. Scaling to $\sigma=c\tau$ gives $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$. Thus $\Phi$ is $C^2$, its four derivative columns are $n,e_1,e_2,e_3$, and its determinant in the chart is $\gamma>0$. Its inverse is explicit from $t=x^0/c$, $\xi=x^1-q(t)$, $y=x^2,z=x^3$, so it is injective with open image and satisfies the precise $J\times B\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ family hypothesis of [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]. The $C^1$ field $n$ depends only on $t=x^0/c$. Using the first-order projected formula for $\theta$, and the fact that $s_\parallel$ is horizontal, Writing $\dot\beta=d\beta/dt$, the only nonzero coordinate derivatives are $\partial_0n_0=-\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$ and $\partial_0n_1=\gamma^3\dot\beta/c$. Therefore $s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3\beta\dot\beta/c$, giving $\theta(s_\parallel,s_\parallel)=s_\parallel^a s_\parallel^b\partial_an_b=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^3$. This proves the formula with exactly $C^2$ data and agrees with [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]](d); it does not require a smooth-only supplier for the nonsmooth branch.
(c) Compute $h(e,e)=1+\gamma^2\beta^2=\gamma^2$ and $h(e)=e+\gamma\beta n=\gamma s_\parallel$. Since $\theta(n,\cdot)=0$, the difference of $e/\gamma$ and $s_\parallel$ is annihilated by $\theta$. Applying [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] to the four-dimensional family, then restricting to fixed transverse labels, gives $G=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^2,1,1)$ and the length/rate identities. Independently $d\gamma/dt=\gamma^3q\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$ and $d/d\tau=\gamma d/dt$ give $d(\gamma L)/d\tau=\gamma^4Lq\prime q\prime\prime/c^2$. The derivative with respect to geometric proper length is instead $d/d\sigma=(\gamma/c)d/dt$. The length $\gamma L$ is exactly the integral of the pulled-back local rest metric over the fixed-label segment; the fixed-$\sigma$ segment need not lie in an endpoint observer's orthogonal hyperplane. The equality/constancy statements follow from $\gamma=(1-q\prime{}^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
(d) Compare $\mathcal L(t)$ with $\mathcal L(0)=\gamma(0)L$. This gives the factor and the stretch/shrink cases without an initial-rest hypothesis. Specializing $q\prime(0)=0$ gives the original initially resting stretch conclusion. Material failure and constitutive stress require an additional model and are not deduced.
(e) Apply the exact smooth Rindler clause of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] and [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]]; its rigidity and unequal radial accelerations provide the stated contrast. (f) Retain all physical qualifications and the absence of empirical or material-dynamics conclusions.

before_consumer.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions for the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let J be an open interval containing 0, let q: J -> R be C^2 with |q'(t)| < c for every t in J, put gamma(t) := (1 - q'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, let L > 0 and a real pair y_0, z_0 be given, and consider the two rocket worldlines x_0(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t), y_0, z_0) and x_L(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + L, y_0, z_0), t in J. Consider also an idealized thread whose material points are labelled by xi in an open interval containing [0,L] and whose element labelled xi moves on the worldline x_xi(t) := x^{-1}(c t, q(t) + xi, y_0, z_0). Then: (a) Kinematics of the rockets. x_0 and x_L are C^2 future timelike worldlines with four-velocity U_xi(t) = gamma(t) (c, q'(t), 0, 0) (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(e)); the two rockets have equal chart-frame velocity q'(t) at every chart time and their chart-frame separation is the constant q(t) + L - q(t) = L, so their chart-frame accelerations q''(t) are equal as well. (b) The translated congruence and its expansion. On the open set covered by the worldlines, n := gamma(t) (1, q'(t)/c, 0, 0) is a smooth future unit timelike field whose flow lines are the worldlines x_xi (which are translated members of one another); it is the translated congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (d), whose unit longitudinal rest vector is s := gamma (q'/c, 1, 0, 0) and whose expansion along s is theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3 (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (c)); this quantity is nonzero exactly at parameter values with q'(t) q''(t) nonzero, and it changes sign with q'q''. (c) Rest separation versus chart separation. The material field e := partial_xi is the unit chart displacement e = (0,1,0,0); its rest length per unit label is |e|_h = sqrt(h(e,e)) = gamma(t), and the rest separation between the two rockets, measured with the material metric of lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching along the flow, is |e|_h L = gamma(t) L. By that lemma the fractional rate of change of the rest separation per unit proper time is c theta(s,s) = gamma^3 q' q''/c^2, so d(gamma L)/dtau = gamma^4 L q' q''/c^2 and, in particular, whenever q'(t) = v at some time, the rest separation at that time equals L/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) > L if v != 0, with minimum L exactly at parameter values with q' = 0. Thus the chart-frame separation L is constant while the rest separation gamma(t) L is not. (d) Material reading of the thread. If a thread attached to the rockets is modelled by material points following the flow lines of n (each thread element moving with the locally coincident rocket), then by lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching its internal longitudinal material metric component is G_11 = gamma(t)^2 and its own rest-length measure between the two endpoint elements grows from L to gamma(t) L; whenever q'(t) != 0 the thread is stretched relative to its initial length by the factor gamma(t) > 1. A conclusion that an actual thread breaks or is under a definite tension requires an elasticity model with a failure or constitutive criterion; no such model is specified here, and no breaking or tension conclusion is drawn from the kinematic computation alone. (e) Contrast with Born rigidity. The Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b) is Born rigid, its neighbouring worldlines have constant rest separation, and its proper accelerations c^2/rho are unequal (def-sr-proper-acceleration); conversely the translated congruence has equal chart-frame velocity and acceleration profiles along its members but is not Born rigid wherever q'q'' != 0. Born rigidity of a congruence is therefore not equivalent to equality of the chart-frame accelerations of its members, and constant chart separation of a family of worldlines is not the constancy of their rest separation. No choice principle is used.

Let $\pi:E\to M$ be a smooth vector bundle. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be smooth, with smooth local extensions at any included endpoints. Give
$$\gamma^*E=\{(t,e)\in I\times E:\gamma(t)=\pi(e)\}$$
the subspace topology. For a bundle chart $\Phi:E|_U\to U\times\mathbb R^r$, writing $\Phi(e)=(\pi(e),v)$, the pulled-back chart and its inverse are
$$ (t,e)\longmapsto(t,v),\qquad (t,v)\longmapsto\bigl(t,\Phi^{-1}(\gamma(t),v)\bigr).$$
They are continuous for the subspace and product topologies, and the overlap maps are $(t,v)\mapsto(t,g_{\beta\alpha}(\gamma(t))v)$, hence smooth and fibrewise linear. Thus they directly define a smooth rank-$r$ bundle over $I$, with the stated smooth-up-to-endpoint convention. The interval $I$, as a subspace of $\mathbb R$, and the manifold $E$ are Hausdorff and second countable. Their product is Hausdorff by [[lem-products-preserve-t0-t1-and-hausdorff]], and products of their two fixed countable bases form a countable basis. Hence both properties pass to the subspace $\gamma^*E$ by [[lem-t0-t1-and-hausdorff-are-hereditary]] and [[prop-second-countability-is-hereditary]].

A **section of $E$ along $\gamma$** is a smooth section of this bundle $\gamma^*E$. Equivalently it is a smooth map $V:I\to E$ with $\pi(V(t))=\gamma(t)$. For $E=TM$ it is a **vector field along $\gamma$**. In a pulled-back frame it has the form $V(t)=\sum_jv^j(t)e_j(\gamma(t))$ with arbitrary smooth coefficients $v^j$.

Values belong to the fibre over the parameter value, even if $\gamma(t)=\gamma(u)$ for $t\ne u$. For example, for a constant curve at $p$ and $v\ne0$ in $E_p$, the section $V(t)=tv$ is allowed and cannot be $s\circ\gamma$ for an ambient section $s$. Thus an ambient extension is not part of this definition.

For a piecewise smooth curve on a compact interval, use a finite subdivision into smooth pieces (each smooth up to its endpoints). A piecewise smooth section is continuous on the whole interval and smooth on each piece. On a singleton interval it is just a fibre vector; on an empty interval it is the empty section. These conventions define sections, without attempting differentiation on a singleton.

$$q_{f,c} : A \setminus \{c\} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad q_{f,c}(x) := \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c)$ omits $c$, so

$$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap A \;=\; N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap (A \setminus \{c\}) ,$$

and the left-hand side is nonempty because $c$ is a limit point of $A$. So
$q_{f,c}$ is a function on a set having $c$ as a limit point, and
$\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x)$ is a notion that [[def-function-limit]] defines.

$f$ is **differentiable at $c$** when that limit exists, and then the
**derivative of $f$ at $c$** is

$$f'(c) \;:=\; \lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) \;=\; \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

**Two obligations are carried by that notation, and both are discharged here.**

1. **Uniqueness.** Writing $f'(c)$ treats the right-hand side as a name for a
   single real number. That is legitimate: $c$ is a limit point of the domain
   $A \setminus \{c\}$ of $q_{f,c}$, so at most one real can satisfy the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, by [[lem-function-limit-unique]] applied to
   $q_{f,c}$. Two reals both meeting the condition are therefore equal, and the
   symbol denotes.
2. **Meaningfulness.** The hypothesis that $c$ is a limit point of $A$ is not
   decoration. At an **isolated** point of $A$ the punctured condition
   $0 < |x - c| < \delta$ is met by no point of the domain at all, so the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula is satisfied vacuously by *every* real at
   once; this is why [[def-function-limit]] leaves the limit undefined there,
   and it is why this library defines $f'(c)$ only at a limit point of $A$. At
   an isolated point of its domain a function is neither differentiable nor
   non-differentiable here: the question is not posed.

**The limit sees only $A \setminus \{c\}$, so how the difference quotient is
extended to $c$ is irrelevant.** Let $Q : A \to \mathbb{R}$ agree with
$q_{f,c}$ at every point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, and let $L \in \mathbb{R}$.
Then $\lim_{x \to c} Q(x) = L$ if and only if $\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) = L$.
Both conditions read: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ such that every point $x$ of the relevant domain with
$0 < |x - c| < \delta$ satisfies $|{\cdot} - L| < \varepsilon$
([[def-function-limit]]). The clause $0 < |x - c|$ removes $x = c$ from both
quantifiers, so in both cases the points quantified over are exactly the
$x \in A \setminus \{c\}$ with $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, at which $Q$ and
$q_{f,c}$ take the same value. The two conditions are the same condition.

**Differentiability on a set.** For $S \subseteq A$, $f$ is **differentiable on
$S$** when it is differentiable at every $c \in S$; implicit in that phrase is
that every point of $S$ is a limit point of $A$. $f$ is **differentiable** when
it is differentiable on the whole of $A$.

**Restriction of the domain.** Let $B \subseteq A$, let $c \in B$ and suppose
$c$ is a limit point of $B$. If $f$ is differentiable at $c$, then so is the
restriction $f|_B : B \to \mathbb{R}$, and

$$(f|_B)'(c) \;=\; f'(c) .$$

Indeed $B \setminus \{c\} \subseteq A \setminus \{c\}$; the displayed identity
of punctured neighbourhoods above, applied to $B$, shows that $c$ is a limit
point of $B \setminus \{c\}$; the difference quotient $q_{f|_B, c}$ is the
restriction of $q_{f,c}$ to $B \setminus \{c\}$, since $f|_B(c) = f(c)$; and
claim 2 of [[lem-limit-is-local]] carries the limit to that restriction.

**Every point of a nondegenerate interval is a limit point of it.** Let
$J \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) with at least two
elements and let $p \in J$. Choose $q \in J$ with $q \ne p$, and let a real
$\varepsilon > 0$ be given. If $p < q$, put $y := p + \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ q - p\}$;
then $p < y$, and $y - p \le \tfrac{1}{2}(q-p) < q - p$, so $p < y < q$ and
order-convexity gives $y \in J$, while $0 < |y - p| < \varepsilon$. If $q < p$,
the point $y := p - \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ p - q\}$ serves in the same
way. So $N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(p) \cap J \ne \varnothing$ for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$, that is, $p$ is a limit point of $J$
([[def-limit-point-r]]).

Consequently, for $f$ defined on a nondegenerate interval $I$, the symbol
$f'(c)$ is meaningful at **every** $c \in I$, endpoints included. At an endpoint
the difference quotient is taken over the points of $I$ lying on the one side
that is available, so what other texts call a one-sided derivative is, here,
simply the derivative of $f$ on $I$.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

supplier_registry.exact_interface:
Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
([[def-interior-closure-boundary-r]], [[def-derivative]]), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.
